Taught programmes
Taught programmes
Before applying for a taught programme at the University, ensure that you can meet all of the University’s minimum entry requirements. The information below includes details on how and when to apply for our taught programmes.
Please note that for us to begin processing your application, payment of the £50 (pounds sterling) fee is required, except for postgraduate online programmes.
You will need to complete the payment process before you submit your application. In some circumstances students may be considered for an application fee waiver.
If you are interested in studying a research programme, visit the research programmes page for details on how to apply.
If you have any questions about postgraduate study, please ask Admissions.
Application information
Open all
Applying
You can apply online, save your progress and continue working on your application before you submit it.
How to apply
To apply, please go to your course page where you will find an online application link for your chosen course.
When to apply
Applications open at the start of August each year and close at different points depending on the programme you apply to. Check your programme page for the deadline.
You should apply as early as possible. This will give you time to apply for scholarships, accommodation, and a visa (if applicable).
You can apply before you have been awarded your undergraduate degree. The University can make you a conditional offer based on receiving a specific mark for your degree, you do not need to wait to graduate before you apply.
Application deadlines
Most taught Masters programmes:
start in September of each year
close for applications on Thursday 5 August 2027
Some programmes have alternative start dates and application deadlines. Check the dates on the specific programme page for your course.
Your application
When reviewing your application, the University will consider:
any previously studied qualifications
any individual modules you have studied
any work or professional experience that could be relevant to your application
any extracurricular activities that may be relevant to your intended programme of study
your personal statement
your CV
your academic reference or references
your writing sample (if applicable)
any extenuating circumstances
If you have not yet applied, ask your referee to include information about any extenuating circumstances in their reference, and include any documentation you may have in your application. After you have applied, you can email documentation to pgt.application@st-andrews.ac.uk.
Notification
The University will notify you when there is a decision on your application. We aim for this to take around three weeks after your application is complete.
Decisions on applications for programmes such as Psychology and MSc Marine Mammal Science will be made after the application deadline. This is because these programmes use a gathered field approach, where all applications are collected before being assessed.
An incomplete application or missing required documents will delay the decision.
Multiple courses
You can apply for multiple courses, but you cannot specify if you prefer one course or another.
If you want to apply for more than one course, you should complete a separate application form for each course.
It is not possible to study two courses at the same time and it is unlikely that you could take a class from another course and have it count towards your credit load.
Students can sometimes audit classes from another course with approval from the course coordinator.
If you are applying to the Business School you should only submit one application as the most suitable course will be offered to you.
Problems when applying
You should email pgt.application@st-andrews.ac.uk if:
you have a problem when you apply
you can’t upload your documents, attach them in your email and quote your application ID number
you make a mistake in your application to explain what you would like to change
Entry requirements
To study a taught programme you’ll normally need a good first degree with Honours from a UK university, or its overseas equivalent.
Not all degree programmes require prior experience, but some require you to have studied a certain subject or range of subjects, so it is important that you check your individual course page.
Read the entry requirements and country information for more details about the qualifications we accept and the required grades.
You must provide your qualification documents in their original language and a translated copy of each into English if this is not the original language. The translation needs verification that it is certified by a qualified individual or organisation. This must include the full name and contact details of the individual or organisation who made the translation.
We do not require the GMAT or the GRE.
In more complex cases we cannot assess qualifications in full before you submit your application. If you are unsure whether your qualifications meet the entry requirements, or if you think you do not have the grades specified, we encourage you to apply. All applications are assessed on a case-by-case basis taking into account all information provided to us, not just your grades.
English language requirements
Whether you will need to provide an English language test score to evidence your English language ability depends on your educational background. Read the English language requirements page for full details.
An English language test result is not required when you first apply. We will review your background to see if you meet our English language requirements. If you do not meet these requirements, any offer would include a condition for you to achieve a specific score in an English language test.
Research skills
Applicants to the following programmes must also complete a research skills section. The online application includes a number of questions and free-text boxes for your responses.
Animal Behaviour (MSc)
Astrophysics (MSc)
Marine Ecosystem Management (MSc)
Marine Mammal Science (MSc)
Supporting documents and references
Check the course page for all the documents you’ll need when you apply.
You must submit your documents using the applicant portal. You will need to submit the required documents before your application can be considered. Your application form will guide you on what documents are required for your programme.
Required documents for most courses
an up-to-date academic transcript and your degree certificates with an explanation of the grading scale and Honours classification at the awarding institution. Please only upload certified copies with official English translations, if applicable. Do not send original transcripts or degree certificates as they cannot be returned
a CV that includes your personal details with a history of your education and employment to date
a personal statement
a signed academic reference
evidence of English language proficiency  is required if English is not your first language. If you haven’t taken an English language test, you can submit your result after you apply. Any University offer will be conditional on you providing evidence of the required English language score for your programme.
Some programmes might want to see a sample of academic written work, though not all programmes require this. Check application requirements on the course webpage for your chosen programme.
The sample:
can be an extract from a previous project or essay, or part of your undergraduate dissertation
must be written in English
does not need to include notes from being marked
does not need to have been published
The sample must be written by you. If you want to include a piece of work with more than one author, you should include a section that only you wrote.
The sample should be as close to 2,000 words as possible. You can use a few more words to provide context if you need to, but if the sample is considerably longer the School may only consider a sample that approximates 2,000 words. The sample is used to assess your writing style. The 2,000-word limit does not include bibliography, reference list or footnotes.
To meet the conditions of your offer, you should submit the documents required in the conditions of your offer by 21 August in the year of entry. If you require a visa to study in the UK you must provide evidence to meet the conditions of your offer before this deadline, so that you can start your course in September.
References
You must provide a reference with your application. Some programmes may ask for a second reference. If you cannot provide any academic references, please contact the School you are applying to.
Your reference must include your full name and proposed programme of study. The University cannot make a decision on your application until the reference has been submitted.
Your referee
When you apply, the University will normally email your referee to request an academic reference. You are responsible for making sure that your referee sends their references to the University.
Your referee can either:
upload their reference using our online system
email their reference to pgt.application@st-andrews.ac.uk from their own email address
A referee may use their own headed paper.
If you are applying for more than one programme each application must contain a copy of your supporting documents. A reference is required for each programme application.
Important dates and deadlines
The majority of taught Masters programmes will start in September of each year, with the exception of some online courses and the following programmes which have additional entry points:
MSc Artificial Intelligence
MSc Computer Science
MSc Software Engineering
MSc, PGDip, PGCert Teaching English to speakers of other languages (TESOL)
MSc, PGDip, PGCert International Education
MSc, PGDip, PGCert Digital Education
Application closing dates vary depending on the programme you are applying for and whether you are applying for scholarship funding. Please refer to the appropriate subject page for these deadlines. Some programmes will close before the deadline if the course is full. In all cases, early application is advisable. This is to allow sufficient time to process our decision and, importantly, to give you time to obtain visas, apply for scholarships and organise travel arrangements, if needed.
Decisions normally take around three weeks once all supporting documents and references have been received and the application is complete with the exception of the MSc Psychology (Conversion) and MSc Marine Mammal Science when decisions will be sent out after the closing date.
For offer holders, the deadline to meet any offer conditions is 21 August (to start studies in September), 30 November (to begin studies in January), or five working days after the offer is made, whichever is latest in the year of entry, or otherwise specified in the offer letter.
Fees and funding
Tuition fees will vary depending on what programme you are studying and where you are from.
You may be able to apply for help with funding your studies at the University. Early application is strongly advised if you are considering applying for a scholarship. Many have an early closing date, often between December and February, and you should check the application deadlines carefully for any funding that you are interested in applying to. After you have submitted your application to study at the University, you can apply for any scholarships that you are eligible for – please note, you do not need to have received an offer of a place first to be able to apply.
We continue to accept self-funded applications even after scholarship deadlines have passed. If you need further guidance on this, please contact the Admissions team.
For more advice on scholarships and funding, please refer to our scholarships catalogue.
Postgraduate taught application fee
In order for us to begin processing your application, payment of an application fee of £50 (pounds sterling) is required. You will need to complete the payment process in the application form when you submit your application.
Applications for the University's online postgraduate programmes are exempt from this application fee.
Application fee waivers
The application fee will be waived in the following circumstances.
UK-domiciled applicants
The application fee will be waived for applicants:
in receipt of means-tested scholarship or maintenance grant as an undergraduate student
who are first generation in family to pursue undergraduate study
have been in local authority care
have been involved in national widening access schemes
have caring responsibilities
Applicants with asylum seeker, refugee or humanitarian protection status
The application fee will be waived for applicants who have a valid Asylum Registration Card or relevant Biometric Residence Permit.
International applicants domiciled in low-income countries and territories
The application fee will be waived for applicants who are domiciled in low-income countries and territories as defined by the OECD least-developed and low-income country and territory and World Bank low-income country and territory lists.
Requests for the application fee to be waived for any other reason can be made by contacting the Admissions team.
Applicants with special needs or disabilities
Applicants can disclose the details of any disabilities or specific learning needs that they have in the relevant section of the application form. The University’s Disability team will review this information.
You can declare a disability or long-term medical condition before or after starting your course, but the University cannot guarantee that resources will be available when you arrive if you don’t declare before you start. Complete this online form to contact the Advice and Support Centre (ASC) as soon as you can to ensure the University will have enough time to make reasonable adjustments.
Applications are assessed purely on academic merit. The impact of a disability will be considered only after a final decision has been made on your application.
